newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-Paris to Asia rates seen stable after Air France rises.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Paris to Asia rates seen stable after Air France rises.

text.p: The withdrawal of fuel surcharges mid-April gave Air France scope to increase ex-Paris rates on some key Far East routes earlier this month but overall these look stable till the autumn, a Reuter survey showed.
The French carrier increased rates to Hong Kong and Tokyo by 50 centimes a kg, effective May 15.
The increases work out at almost six percent for Hong Kong and just over three percent to Tokyo, an Air France Cargo official told Reuters.
"While these increases reflect buoyant demand, particularly to Hong Kong, they are partly a consequence of us withdrawing our fuel surcharge," the official said.
Neither Cathay Pacific Airways nor Japan Airlines the major maindeck carriers from Paris to Hong Kong and Tokyo, along with Air France, had applied the fuel surcharge, the official added.

"Withdrawing the surcharge changed the "parity" between our rates and some of the other airlines. For example, on the Tokyo route our rates were a little below those of JAL so the increase more or less brought them into line with theirs."
Air France, which operates a twice-weekly freighter service to had also increased ex-Paris rates on the route by 50 centimes a kg, the equivalent of around six percent, effective May 1.

"In the case of Taipei, the increases are more indicative of favourable market conditions - the fuel surcharge being less of a factor in that the other major carrier on the route, Taiwanese Eva Air, like ourselves, applied it and then withdrew it."
For its part, Eva Air said it ex-Paris rates would remain unchanged despite Air France's rise and buoyant demand on the route currently.
The carrier flies a three times weekly Boeing 747 combi service between Paris and Taipei via Vienna and Bangkok.
The combis are scheduled to be replaced by 747 passenger aircraft during the peak tourist season -- starting on June 19 --before returning on a permanent basis from September 19.
Eva Air's Paris cargo station has a 10-tonne per flight allocation on a twice-weekly MD-11 freighter service from Brussels to Taipei, launched earlier in May.
In a recent report published by cargo consultancy, MergeGlobal Inc, Air France displaced Lufthansa as the capacity leader among scheduled carriers in the Europe-Asia airfreight market.
MergeGlobal said Air France was the capacity leader in three market sub-categories: Europe-to-North Asia, North Asia to Europe and Southeast Asia to Europe.
Air France aside, there appears to have been little movement in rates over the past month and the outlook is now for stability until the autumn.

One exception could be Korean Airlines (KAL), which is contemplating increases in July following modest rises in April. "The market is strong at the moment and capacity is becoming tighter - the right kind of market conditions for increases. "

"However, with the prospect of an additional frequency on our Paris-Seoul freighter service taking the weekly number to three in co-operation with Air France in the autumn, it would perhaps be a delicate move and we have not yet finalised our decision," a CDG-based KAL cargo official said.
The Paris-Seoul service had been bolstered by the growing trend among shippers to seek direct routes for their goods in preference to transporting them via transhipment, the official added.

"The Korean economy had gone into a bit of a recession and while the volume of industrial goods we are shipping remains a little flat, consumer products, such as perfumes and cosmetics, are flourishing," the official said.

Meanwhile, on another prime Far East route, Paris-Tokyo, Japan Airlines, JAL, which partners Air France on several full-freighter flights, describes current load factors as "average" and at a similar level to the same period last year.

"This is traditional market behaviour at this time of the year, April and May not being very strong months for export traffic to Japan. We expect demand to pick up again in June as is normally the case," says JAL cargo manager, France, Francis Clement.
He added: "As far as rates are concerned, there are no adjustments are planned before the autumn."
JAL' last ex-Paris rates increases dates back to January 1997.

In the Indian sub-Continent sector, a strategic alliance between Air France and Air India will include freight co-operation. This will also extend to Air India having access to cargo capacity on Air France's European passenger flight network and trucking services.
Air France is to allocate three pallets of cargo space to Air India on each of its seven weekly Boeing 747-200F services between Paris and India, effective from the 1997/98 winter season.
Air France operates B747F services from Paris to Delhi, Bombay,Bangalore and Madras.
Independent of the Air France alliance, Air India recently-announced it was to increase cargo capacity significantly on its Paris/CDG-Delhi route.

"As part of Air India's policy to cut passenger and cargo capacity from Europe, our services from Paris have been progressively reduced from five 747 passenger flights and a DC8 freighter per week to two 747 passenger flights per week currently," an Air India cargo official told Reuters.
The service' full routing reads Paris-Frankfurt-Delhi Bombay.

"However, the indications are that the market cargo has begun to pick up again and B747-300 combis will replace the B747 passenger aircraft on the route from June 1. A third passenger flight will be added from July 1 too," he added.

Cargo capacity will be shared with Air India's Frankfurt station, and although the combis will more than double ex-Paris capacity, "we do not expect this to trigger off a downturn in rates. This have been increased by between 20 and 40 percent over the past eight to nine months, largely as a result of a under-capacity and are now generally." --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
